newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale says barley vote results out in March.
newsitem.headline: Goodale says barley vote results out in March.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Monday he expected the results of a farmers' vote on the Canadian Wheat Board's monopoly over barley exports to be released in March.
Ballots were sent out last month by KPMG Chartered Accountants, who are administering the vote, which asked if the board's role in barley exports should end.
"When they're ready with their arithmetic we'll release it right away," said Goodale. "They have said that they project somewhere between the second and third week of March."

Canada is the second biggest supplier of wheat to the world market. About 30 percent of barley grown on the Prairies is exported, with the balance fed to livestock or used in brewing in Canada. Debate has been fierce over whether farmers would be better off without the board.
Some farmers have criticized the question as being all or nothing, not allowing a system where some grain could be exported privately and some through the board.
